title: Toronto Trivia Night

questions.q: What is the name of Toronto's NHL team?
The Toronto Blue Jays won back-to-back World Series titles in which two years?
In which year did the Toronto Raptors win their first NBA championship?
Which Great Lake lies along Toronto's waterfront?
The CN Tower takes its initials from which company, which built it?
Which Toronto-born rapper did most to popularise the nickname "The 6"?
Before it was incorporated as a city in 1834, Toronto was known by what name?
The Hall of Fame for which sport is in downtown Toronto, partly housed in an old bank building?
Toronto's famous peameal bacon is rolled in what today?
What was the Rogers Centre called when it opened in 1989?

notes: Toronto Maple Leafs; see NHL.com team page.
1992 and 1993 World Series; see MLB.com World Series history.
2019 NBA Finals, beat Golden State; see NBA.com Finals history.
Lake Ontario; see City of Toronto waterfront pages or any atlas.
Built by Canadian National Railway, opened 1976; see the CN Tower's official history page.
Drake, born in Toronto 1986, popularised 'The 6' around his 2016 album Views; see Drake (Wikipedia) or Toronto nicknames coverage.
Town of York renamed Toronto on incorporation, 6 March 1834; see City of Toronto 'Toronto history' pages.
Hockey Hall of Fame, Brookfield Place, includes the former Bank of Montreal building at Yonge and Front; see hhof.com.
Originally rolled in ground dried peas, now cornmeal; see Peameal bacon (Wikipedia) or St. Lawrence Market history.
Opened as SkyDome in June 1989, renamed Rogers Centre in 2005; see MLB.com Blue Jays ballpark history.
